title: What Happened When 8 Sane People Pretended to Be Mentally Ill - Documentary - Rosenhan Experiment

sentences.en: What if your professional expertise could earn you money even when you're not working?
sentences.zh: 如果你的专业知识即使在你没工作时也能为你赚钱，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and since 2019 I've been building additional income streams
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家Marianne Trent博士，自2019年以来，我一直在建立额外的收入来源，

sentences.en: through books, online courses, and memberships, and it's made such a difference to my business and my life.
sentences.zh: 通过书籍、在线课程和会员制，这给我的事业和生活带来了巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Tonight at 7pm, Sophie Foote is hosting a free Make Money Online Masterclass, exploring how you can turn your existing skills and knowledge into additional income streaMs.
sentences.zh: 今晚7点，Sophie Foote将举办一场免费的“在线赚钱大师班”，探讨如何将你现有的技能和知识转化为额外的收入来源。

sentences.en: And I'd love more psychologists and mental health professionals to join us.
sentences.zh: 我非常希望更多的心理学家和心理健康专业人士能加入我们。

sentences.en: I'll be there too, supporting a lovely community of fellow psychologists, exploring what's possible beyond one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我也会参加，支持一个可爱的心理学家同行社区，探索一对一工作之外的可能性。

sentences.en: Replays are available if you can't join live.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法参加直播，可以观看回放。

sentences.en: Click the link with this pre-roll or reach out to me on socials to grab your free place, because you can serve others and deserve financial freedom too.
sentences.zh: 点击此片头视频中的链接，或在社交媒体上联系我以获取免费名额，因为你既可以服务他人，也理应获得财务自由。

sentences.en: How do you tell the difference between someone who is sane and someone who isn't?
sentences.zh: 你如何区分一个人是精神正常还是不正常？

sentences.en: What if the system itself can't even tell?
sentences.zh: 如果连系统本身都无法区分呢？

sentences.en: In the 1970s, a daring experiment put mental health institutions to the test, and the results shook the psychiatric world.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，一项大胆的实验对精神卫生机构进行了测试，结果震惊了整个精神病学界。

sentences.en: Today, we are exploring what's known as the Rosenhawn Experiment, and uncovering what it taught us then and now about perception, diagnosis, and mental health.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨所谓的“罗森汉恩实验”，并揭示它在当时和现在教会了我们关于感知、诊断和心理健康的什么道理。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Dr Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是Marianne Trent博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Welcome along.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看。

sentences.en: In today's episode, we are diving into one of the most iconic and controversial studies in psychology.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将深入探讨心理学中最具标志性和争议性的研究之一。

sentences.en: That is, David Rosenhawn's On Being Sane in Insane Places.
sentences.zh: 那就是大卫·罗森汉恩的《精神错乱场所中的理智》。

sentences.en: And honestly, since I first learned about this study when I was in my A-levels, that name has stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 老实说，自从我在A-level课程中第一次了解到这项研究以来，这个名字就一直印在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: It really is iconic.
sentences.zh: 它确实非常具有标志性。

sentences.en: And that's because this experiment challenged the very foundations of psychiatric diagnosis and revealed somewhat uncomfortable truths at times
sentences.zh: 这是因为该实验挑战了精神病学诊断的基础，并揭示了一些有时令人不安的真相，

sentences.en: about how mental health care was being practiced.
sentences.zh: 关于心理健康护理是如何实践的。

sentences.en: We are going to be breaking down what happened, what it means, and how it's still relevant today.
sentences.zh: 我们将剖析发生了什么、这意味着什么，以及它在今天有何现实意义。

sentences.en: Let's dive in.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: The experiment, what happened?
sentences.zh: 实验，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So it was 1973, and David Rosenhawn, who's a psychologist and professor, set out to answer a bold question.
sentences.zh: 那是1973年，心理学家兼教授大卫·罗森汉恩着手回答一个大胆的问题。

sentences.en: Can mental health professionals reliably distinguish between what he was calling sanity and insanity?
sentences.zh: 精神健康专业人员能否可靠地分辨出他所称的“理智”与“疯狂”？

sentences.en: To test this, Rosenhawn recruited eight pseudo-patients, which, incidentally, did actually include himself.
sentences.zh: 为了测试这一点，罗森汉恩招募了八名伪病人，顺便提一下，其中确实包括他自己。

sentences.en: These people were from various professions, including psychologists, even a psychiatrist, a housewife, a painter.
sentences.zh: 这些人来自各种职业，包括心理学家、甚至还有一位精神科医生、一位家庭主妇和一位画家。

sentences.en: And what they were tasked with was to all pretend to experience one symptom.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是假装经历一种症状。

sentences.en: In this case, he asked them to report that they were hearing voices and that these voices said thud, empty, or hollow.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他要求他们报告说他们听到了声音，这些声音说的是“砰”、“空”或“中空”。

sentences.en: Rosenhawn specifically chose those words because he thought they didn't align with any known psychiatric symptoms at that time.
sentences.zh: 罗森汉恩特意选择了这些词，因为他认为它们在当时与任何已知的精神病症状都不吻合。

sentences.en: They weren't commonly reported words for any diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 它们不是任何诊断中常用的词汇。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: What were the results?
sentences.zh: 结果如何？

sentences.en: Well, all eight were admitted to inpatient hospitals, and most of them were diagnosed with schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所有八个人都被送进了住院医院，其中大多数人被诊断为精神分裂症。

sentences.en: The study really began, though, when they had managed to get themselves admitted to those psychiatric hospitals.
sentences.zh: 然而，这项研究真正的开始，是当他们成功让自己住进那些精神病院之后。

sentences.en: Thereafter, the patients, the pseudo-patients, I should say, were asked to behave completely normally.
sentences.zh: 此后，这些病人，或者我应该说是伪病人，被要求表现得完全正常。

sentences.en: They didn't report any additional symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 他们没有报告任何额外的症状。

sentences.en: They answered all questions that were asked to them.
sentences.zh: 他们回答了所有问他们的问题。

sentences.en: And they seemed to have stopped experiencing those auditory hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 而且他们似乎已经停止经历那些听觉幻觉了。

sentences.en: So how long were they in there for?
sentences.zh: 那么他们在里面待了多久呢？

sentences.en: Well, the average length of stay was 19 days, but with one person even staying for 52 days.
sentences.zh: 平均住院时间为19天，但其中一人甚至待了52天。

sentences.en: Despite acting sane inside the hospitals, none of the staff identified them as imposters.
sentences.zh: 尽管在医院里表现得理智，但没有一个工作人员认出他们是冒充者。

sentences.en: But interestingly, many of the real patients did suspect that they weren't truly ill.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，许多真正的病人确实怀疑他们并没有真正生病。

sentences.en: They would say things to them like, you're not crazy, are you?
sentences.zh: 他们会对他们说诸如“你没疯，对吧？”之类的话。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry if any of the language in this video is triggering.
sentences.zh: 如果这个视频中的任何语言让你感到不适，我深表歉意。

sentences.en: It's the language that was used in the 1970s at the time.
sentences.zh: 这是20世纪70年代当时所使用的语言。

sentences.en: Psychological insights.
sentences.zh: 心理学见解。

sentences.en: What did we learn?
sentences.zh: 我们学到了什么？

sentences.en: One, the power of labels.
sentences.zh: 第一，标签的力量。

sentences.en: Once the pseudo-patients were labelled with a psychiatric diagnosis, everything else they did was interpreted through that lens.
sentences.zh: 一旦伪病人被贴上精神病诊断的标签，他们所做的一切都会通过这个视角来解读。

sentences.en: For example, they were asked to record their notes of what was going on in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们被要求记录下医院里发生的事情。

sentences.en: That note-taking, that just writing things down in a journal, in a diary, was described as pathological writing behaviour.
sentences.zh: 那种记笔记的行为，仅仅是在日记或日志中写下东西，就被描述为“病态的书写行为”。

sentences.en: That's like you writing notes in a meeting, or in a supervision, or writing a diary, or a journal.
sentences.zh: 这就像你在会议中、督导中记笔记，或者写日记、写日志一样。

sentences.en: But these normal actions, that many of us still do, even to this day, were reframed to fit the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 但是这些我们许多人至今仍在做的正常行为，却被重新定义以符合诊断。

sentences.en: They saw what they wanted to see and interpreted it accordingly.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了他们想看到的东西，并据此进行了相应的解读。

sentences.en: Two, confirmation bias.
sentences.zh: 第二，确认偏误。

sentences.en: Staff members' expectations influenced how they perceived the pseudo-patients.
sentences.zh: 工作人员的期望影响了他们对伪病人的感知。

sentences.en: They saw what they expected to see, which is symptoms of mental illness, and dismissed any evidence that seemed to contradict their assumptions or their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了他们期望看到的东西，即精神疾病的症状，并驳回了任何似乎与他们的假设或信念相矛盾的证据。

sentences.en: Three, dehumanisation in psychiatric care.
sentences.zh: 第三，精神护理中的非人性化。

sentences.en: Many of the pseudo-patients reported feeling ignored or treated dismissively.
sentences.zh: 许多伪病人报告说感到被忽视或受到冷遇。

sentences.en: It seemed that doctors and nurses often seemed to avoid direct interactions with the pseudo-patients,
sentences.zh: 医生和护士似乎经常避免与伪病人进行直接互动，

sentences.en: which highlighted what we call the depersonalisation that can seem to occur in institutional settings at times.
sentences.zh: 这突显了我们所说的在机构环境中时常发生的“去人格化”。

sentences.en: The fallout and the controversy.
sentences.zh: 后果与争议。

sentences.en: The study's publication caused somewhat of a furore in the psychiatric community.
sentences.zh: 该研究的发表在精神病学界引起了一阵骚动。

sentences.en: It seemed to reveal cracks in the reliability of psychiatric diagnoses and raised questions about how patients were being treated at that time.
sentences.zh: 它似乎揭示了精神病学诊断可靠性方面的裂痕，并引发了关于当时病人如何被对待的质疑。

sentences.en: Following on from the study, one hospital actually challenged Rosenhan to send more pseudo-patients, claiming that they could identify them.
sentences.zh: 在该研究之后，一家医院实际上向罗森汉恩发起挑战，要求他再派一些伪病人，声称他们能够识别出来。

sentences.en: Over a period of weeks, the staff flagged 41, yes, 41, individuals as imposters.
sentences.zh: 在几周的时间里，工作人员标记了41名，没错，是41名，个人为冒充者。

sentences.en: The twist in the tale?
sentences.zh: 故事的反转？

sentences.en: Rosenhan hadn't sent anyone.
sentences.zh: 罗森汉恩根本没有派任何人去。

sentences.en: Whilst the study was groundbreaking, it wasn't without criticism.
sentences.zh: 虽然这项研究具有开创性，但并非没有批评。

sentences.en: Some argued that the lack of transparency in the methodology used made the results hard to replicate.
sentences.zh: 一些人认为，所用方法论缺乏透明度，使得结果难以复制。

sentences.en: Others believed the study unfairly undermined trust in psychiatric professionals who were doing their best with the knowledge and tools available at the time.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则认为，这项研究不公平地削弱了对精神科专业人员的信任，他们当时正尽其所能利用现有的知识和工具进行工作。

sentences.en: I think an additional consideration would be the waste of psychiatric professionals' time, money and resources too.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个需要考虑的问题是精神科专业人员的时间、金钱和资源的浪费。

sentences.en: Modern relevance.
sentences.zh: 现代意义。

sentences.en: Why does it matter today?
sentences.zh: 为什么它在今天很重要？

sentences.en: Firstly, it gives us food for thought about diagnosis terms and really the ethics of diagnosis
sentences.zh: 首先，它让我们对诊断术语以及作为理解个人及其所经历困难的独立方式的诊断伦理进行了思考。

sentences.en: as a standalone way of understanding people and the difficulties that they experience.
sentences.zh: 当然，虽然自20世纪70年代以来精神病学诊断已经取得了长足的进步，我们有了更完善的标准和工具，如ICD-11和DSM-5。

sentences.en: So, of course, while psychiatric diagnosis has come a long way since the 1970s, we've got more refined criteria and tools like the ICD-11 and the DSM-5.
sentences.zh: 然而，挑战依然存在，特别是在认识心理健康的复杂性和避免过度依赖标签方面。

sentences.en: However, challenges do remain, particularly in recognising the complexity of mental health and avoiding over-reliance on labels.
sentences.zh: 针对精神病学诊断的替代方法，例如由Lucy Johnston和Mary Boyle提出的“权力威胁意义框架”，也已被提出。

sentences.en: Alternative approaches to psychiatric diagnosis, such as the Power Threat Meaning Framework by
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解更多关于“权力威胁意义框架”的信息，请查看《有抱负的心理学家》播客的第21集，我在那一集中与Lucy本人进行了交流。

sentences.en: Lucy Johnston and Mary Boyle, have also been posited.
sentences.zh: 我会在本集的节目说明中提供链接。

sentences.en: And if you'd like to learn more about the Power Threat Meaning Framework, please do check out episode 21 of the Aspiring Psychologist podcast, where I chat with Lucy herself.
sentences.zh: 其次，我们面临着污名化和误诊的问题。

sentences.en: I will link that in the show notes for this episode.
sentences.zh: 这项研究提醒我们，心理健康标签可能会带来污名化。

sentences.en: Secondly, we've got stigma and misdiagnosis.
sentences.zh: 它还强调了寻求第二意见和以病人为中心的护理的重要性，以降低误诊的风险。

sentences.en: The study reminds us of the stigma that can come with mental health labels.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现代精神护理中所知道的是，在后期想要推翻标签和诊断是非常困难的。

sentences.en: It also highlights the importance of second opinions and patient-centred care to reduce the risk of misdiagnosis.
sentences.zh: 而且那种污名化和对你的那种看法可能会伴随你，甚至可能伴随你一生。

sentences.en: Of course, what we know in modern psychiatric care is it can be very hard to get labels and diagnoses overturned at a later stage.
sentences.zh: 第三，我们有心理健康之外的影响。

sentences.en: And that that stigma and that belief about you can follow you around, perhaps throughout your life.
sentences.zh: 这项研究在精神病学之外的见解是，它们适用于任何标签和第一印象影响决策的领域。

sentences.en: Thirdly, we have the implications beyond mental health.
sentences.zh: 这存在于教育、刑事司法或就业中。

sentences.en: The insights from this study, beyond psychiatry, are that they apply to any field where labels and first impressions influence decisions.
sentences.zh: 也许甚至包括社交群体和家庭。

sentences.en: This is around in education, in criminal justice or employment.
sentences.zh: 这确实呼吁我们以同理心和批判性思维来对待每一种情况。

sentences.en: Maybe even social groups and families too.
sentences.zh: 第四点，就现代心理学研究而言，它也为我们的伦理实践和程序提供了参考，并让我们对研究的普遍性进行了思考。

sentences.en: It really is a call for us to approach every situation with empathy and critical thinking.
sentences.zh: 在结束之前，如果你喜欢这一集，你可能也会喜欢我最近对Phineas Gage故事的深入探讨，

sentences.en: And our fourth point, in terms of modern psychology studies, it's also informed our ethical practices
sentences.zh: 那个因脑部受重伤（一根大尖刺穿过大脑）而彻底改变了我们对个性和行为理解的人。

sentences.en: and our procedures and gives us food for thought about the generalizability of research too.
sentences.zh: 我最近还介绍了米尔格拉姆实验，人们因为被告知而对他人实施了大规模的电击。

sentences.en: Before we wrap up, if you are enjoying this episode, you might also love my recent deep dive
sentences.zh: 所以也不要错过那一集。

sentences.en: into the story of Phineas Gage, the man whose brain injury involving a large spike through his brain revolutionised our understanding of personality and behaviour.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让我知道你希望我在未来涵盖哪些主题，我会很高兴。

sentences.en: I also recently covered the Milgram experiment, where people administered massive electric shocks to people because they were told to.
sentences.zh: 请在评论中告诉我。

sentences.en: So don't miss that one either.
sentences.zh: 结论，我们可以从中得到什么？

sentences.en: And I would love it if you would let me know which topics you'd like me to cover in future.
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗森汉恩实验不仅仅是对精神病学诊断的测试。

sentences.en: Do let me know in the comments.
sentences.zh: 它是对我们感知和对待精神疾病方式的大胆挑战。

sentences.en: Conclusion, what can we take away?
sentences.zh: 它提醒我们，标签可以塑造现实，同理心和理解应该始终指导我们对待心理健康护理的方式。

sentences.en: Well, the Rosenhan experiment wasn't just a test of psychiatric diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 那么你对罗森汉恩的研究有什么看法？

sentences.en: It was a bold challenge to the way we perceive and treat mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这是一个必要的警钟吗？

sentences.en: It reminds us that labels can shape reality and that empathy and understanding should always guide our approach to mental health care.
sentences.zh: 还是你认为它越过了伦理界限？

sentences.en: So what do you think of Rosenhan's study?
sentences.zh: 你认为在20世纪70年代，你能够说服自己进入或离开精神病院吗？

sentences.en: Was it a necessary wake-up call?
sentences.zh: 请在下方的评论中告诉我，或者来我的社交媒体上和我聊天，我在那里都是Marianne Trent博士。
